FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institutio n on 25 January 1985, after the draft finalized by the Dye Intermediate Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. 0.2 3,3'-dichlorobenzidine is an important dye intermediate available as its dihydrochloride or monosulphate in the form of wet cake. It is used in the manufacture of organic pigments and dyes. 0.3 3,3'-Dichlorobenzidine structural formulae: and its salts are represented by the following

The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

APPENDIX A ( Table 1, and Clause 5.1 )
METHODS A-l. ASSAY OF TEST FOR 3,3'-DICHLOROBENZIDINE DIHYDROCHLORIDE/SULPHATE

A-1.0 General - Dichlorobenzidine dihydrochloride/sulphate is usually supplied as moist powder. Percent purity shall be determined on dry sample. A-l.1 Determination A-1.1.0 Outline of the Method - It is determined by direct titration involving diazotization of the amine under acidic conditions with standard sodium nitrite'1 solution using starch iodide paper as an indicator ( external ). Procedure - Weigh accurately about 1 *O g of the dry sample in Add 10 ml of a weighing bottle and transfer it into one-litre beaker. Add 60 to 80 ml of distilled water with concentrated hydrochloric acid. Heat it on a hot plate and agitate until sample is a measuring cylinder. dissolved. Do not boil it. Cool to 0 to 5�C by keeping in an ice-bath. Add 0.5 g of potassium bromide. Titrate with sodium nitrite solution making the additions dropwise towards the end of the titration until an immediate blue spot appears on starch iodide paper.

A-2.0 Outline of the Method - The sample is dissolved in an appropriate quantity of hydrochloric acid and tetra-azotized with sodium The resulting solution nitrite solution until tetra-azotization is complete. shall be clear and devoid of any insoluble matter. A-2.1 Reagents Sodium .Nitrite Solution 30 ~percent ( m/v ). 30 percent.

A-2.1.1 A-2.1.2 A-2.1.3

Concentrated Hydrochloric Acid.Starch Iodide Indicator Paper

A-2.2 Procedure - Weigh accurately about 10 g of dry sample ( on the basis of 100 percent freebase ), transfer it to one-litre beaker and add Keep the contents in rapid mechanical agitation, Add 300 ml water. 30 ml of concentrated hydrochloric acid. Agitate for 15 minutes and then cool internally with sufficient amount of crushed ice to obtain a temperature of 0 to 5�C. Also cool it externally by keeping in water-ice Add at once from a burette 18.6 ml of 30 percent sodium mixture. nitrite solution through a long funnel with its tip dipped well below Remove the surface of the solution. Rinse funnel with ice cold water. funnel and continue agitation for 20 minutes at 0 to 5�C throughout. During this interval continually test the solution for excess nitrite with starch iodide indicator paper and excess acid with congo red indicator paper.
NOTE - If it so happens that a nitrite deficiency develops, immediately add 2 ml portion of 30 percent sodium nitrite solution and continue checking for excess nitrite, otherwise tetrazo of dichlorobenzidine immediately forms a dark insoluble matter through coupling reaction. If there is any appreciable amount of insoluble matter, filter solution through a tared gooch crucible ( ML ). Wash beaker with several portions of hydrochloric acid ( 1 : 10 ) and add washing to gooch. Finally wash residue in gooch crucible with 50 ml of hydrochloric acid ( 1 : 10 ). Suck dry and place in the oven at 100�C for 2 hours and then cool in a desiccator. Weigh and repeat the process until constant mass is obtained ( Ms ).

A-3. DETERMINATION
A-3.1

OF ACIDITY

Outline of the Method - The test sample is hydrolyzed with excess alkali and this excess alkali is back titrated against standard acid.

A-3.2 Reagents
A-3.2.1 A-3.2.2 A-3.2.3 A-3.3 Sodium Hydroxide Solution Hydrochloric Acid Solution 1 N 1 N.

Phenolphthalein Indicator Solution

Procedure - Weigh accurately about 1 to 1.5 g of sample on the basis of 100 percent free base and transfer it into 250 ml conical flask. Add 20 ml of sodium hydroxide ( 1 N ) by means of pipette and about Heat the content of the flask till sample under50 ml of distilled water. goes complete hydrolysis. Cool the flask at room temperature and titrate it against hydrochloric acid ( 1 N ) using phenolphthalein as an indicator.
